symbols.name: selected bit count
symbols.meaning: The number of selected address bits that the change acts on, which is also the size of the square matrix M.
symbols.quote: Let $m$ be the number of selected address bits the change acts on.

symbols.name: selected bit column
symbols.meaning: The column vector of the m selected address bits, each an element of the binary field.
symbols.quote: Write $\mathbf b=(b_1,\dots,b_m)$ for the column of those bits, each $b_i\in\mathbb F_2$.

symbols.name: change matrix
symbols.meaning: The invertible m-by-m matrix over the binary field that specifies the change of basis.
symbols.quote: A binary change of basis is specified by an invertible matrix in [Linear algebra basics](linear-algebra-basics.md): a matrix $M$ with an inverse $M^{-1}$, so that $M^{-1}M=I$.

symbols.name: invertible matrices
symbols.meaning: The set of invertible m-by-m matrices over the binary field.
symbols.quote: We write $\mathrm{GL}(m,\mathbb F_2)$ for the set of invertible $m\times m$ matrices over $\mathbb F_2$.

symbols.name: selected address
symbols.meaning: An address of the m selected bits, viewed as a column vector over the binary field.
symbols.quote: Here $\mathbf a\in\mathbb F_2^m$ denotes an address of the $m$ selected bits.

symbols.name: address permutation
symbols.meaning: The permutation of addresses that moves the value at each address a to M a.
symbols.quote: For $M\in\mathrm{GL}(m,\mathbb F_2)$, $P_M$ is the address permutation that moves the value at each address $\mathbf a$ to $M\mathbf a$.

relations.predicate: is specified by an invertible matrix
relations.quote: A binary change of basis is specified by an invertible matrix in [Linear algebra basics](linear-algebra-basics.md): a matrix $M$ with an inverse $M^{-1}$, so that $M^{-1}M=I$.
A binary change of basis is an invertible linear change of coordinates on a block of selected address bits, built over the [binary field](binary-field.md).
